security_frame.attacker: Later-stage Caliptra firmware (FMC or Runtime) executing after an earlier boot stage has provisioned KeyVault entries. The attacker is privileged software at supervisor mode on the Caliptra microcontroller.
security_frame.precondition: An earlier boot stage (ROM, or FMC) has written key material into KeyVault entries and has NOT locked them for use, and the boot flow then advances to the next stage.
security_frame.input: A KeyVault read request from a crypto engine whose dest_valid bit is set for an entry provisioned by the earlier stage.
security_frame.protected_asset: KeyVault key material belonging to a previous boot stage, which the next stage is not entitled to consume.
security_frame.security_property: Stage isolation: on a boot-stage transition, key material that is not part of the next stage's retained set must be cleared atomically, so a later stage cannot consume an earlier stage's assets.
security_frame.implemented_logic: src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:154-164 derives key_entry_clear only from kv_multi_write_err and the software-poked KEY_CTRL.clear bit (itself suppressed by lock_wr/lock_use), and src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:122-123 derives flush_keyvault only from debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch and cptra_in_debug_scan_mode & CLEAR_SECRETS.wr_debug_values. The kv module port list at src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:27-56 carries no boot-stage or boot-policy input, so no per-entry stage-transition clear mask exists.

security_feature_bypassed: Boot-stage asset isolation for the KeyVault: the claim under test is that a hardware transition-clear, with a stable-owner / OCP-lock retention exception set, must wipe non-retained entries when the boot flow advances.
proof_goal: Determine whether the KeyVault retains an unlocked entry's key material across a boot-stage advance in a way that violates a security property this design is actually required to enforce, and whether any stage-transition input exists that could drive such a clear.
minimum_attack_sequence: An earlier boot stage writes key material into a KeyVault entry with a dest_valid bit set for some crypto engine, and leaves lock_use clear.
The boot flow advances to the next stage (ROM to FMC, or FMC to Runtime).
Later-stage firmware programs the crypto engine whose dest_valid bit is set to read that entry.
The engine consumes the earlier stage's key material, which stage isolation should have made unavailable.
expected_evidence: A single-DUT simulation of the kv module that provisions an entry, advances every stage-like input the module actually has, and records whether the entry's data survives and remains readable, together with a control showing the debug/scan flush path does clear it.

A structural audit that enumerates every producer of key_entry_clear and flush_keyvault, every port of the kv module, and every signal in the tree that could represent a boot-stage transition, plus a search of the in-tree specifications for who is assigned the duty of clearing KeyVault entries on a stage transition.
success_criteria: The claim is upheld only if BOTH the simulation shows an earlier stage's key material remains readable after a stage advance AND the audit identifies an in-tree requirement that HARDWARE perform this clear, together with a stage-transition signal that reaches or could reach the kv module.

If the in-tree specifications assign KeyVault clearing on stage transition to ROM or firmware rather than to hardware, and no boot-stage signal exists anywhere in the tree that reaches the KeyVault, then the claim is withdrawn and the case is recorded as false_alarm: the absent logic is not a required hardware feature of this design.

Pre-committed withdrawal: this plan does not claim that fw_update_rst_window is a boot-stage transition marker, and will not treat KeyVault data surviving that window as a violation unless an in-tree statement requires clearing there.
non_findings_intent: Suspected but unproven at plan time: that a boot-stage or lifecycle-stage signal exists in the tree and simply fails to reach the KeyVault. To be checked by enumerating the kv port list and grepping the tree for stage-tracking signals; to be withdrawn if no such signal exists at all.

Suspected but unproven at plan time: that the in-tree specification requires a hardware transition clear. To be checked against the KeyVault configuration document and the hardware and integration specifications; to be withdrawn if those documents assign the duty to ROM or firmware.
